purpose: Fixed synthetic test set for monthly cleanup-model A/B comparison. Mimics Daniel's dictation style (rambling cadence, self-corrections, fillers, domain vocabulary). NEVER edit existing passages — month-over-month comparability depends on the set staying frozen. Add new passages with new ids if needed.

scoring.content_preservation: Every non-filler word in the input must appear in the output in order. Fillers = um, umm, uh, er, ah, hmm ONLY. Words like 'like', 'you know', 'so', 'basically' must be KEPT.
scoring.filler_removal: Pure filler sounds should be removed.
scoring.no_paraphrase: Word substitutions, reordering, or summarization = failure. Dropping an immediately repeated word or phrase is NOT a failure when the repetition is verbatim and adjacent, or separated only by a filler ('not the uh not the' -> 'not the' is acceptable). A self-correction where the speaker changed what they were saying must survive verbatim.
scoring.american_spelling: The cleanup prompt requires American English. British forms in the input (colour, organise, analyse, licence, grey, programme) should appear Americanized in the output. Measured as spelling_fixed %; scored separately from preservation, which normalizes spelling on both sides so an obeyed normalization is never counted as a word substitution. Evidence for the rule: across 503 history entries `colour` survived into cleaned output 9/9 times and -ise verbs were normalized only 5 of 14.
scoring.acceptable_normalizations: Not content loss, and not scored as such: spoken numerals rendered as digits, 'double A' as 'AA', and consecutive words a model correctly writes as one compound proper noun. Spelling normalization per american_spelling is likewise folded before comparison.

changelog.note: Scoring updated: 'umm' added to the filler list, and adjacent verbatim repetition is no longer counted as a paraphrase failure — this mirrors the AICleanupService prompt change of the same date. All seven models in the 2026-08 A/B failed passage 12 identically under the v1 rule, which put a constant +1 in every paraphrase-failure column and cost that metric its ability to discriminate. Passages 16-25 added (real fork vocabulary; the 15-passage set could not resolve the 0.44pp margin between the top two models). NO existing passage was edited. Paraphrase-failure counts are NOT comparable across the v1/v2 boundary; preservation and filler-removal percentages are.

Scoring gains a spelling axis: the cleanup prompt now requires American English, so British forms are normalized on BOTH sides before the preservation comparison (a model obeying the rule must not score as having substituted a word) and a separate spelling_fixed % measures whether it obeyed. Passages 26-27 added with British forms Whisper actually produced in history. NO existing passage was edited. Preservation is comparable across the v2/v3 boundary; spelling_fixed is new.

Scorer folds transcription conventions every model applies: spoken numerals ('large v three turbo' -> 'v3', 'two point two double A' -> '2.2 AA') and compound proper nouns ('weed maps' -> 'Weedmaps'). These were scoring as content loss and produced 3 false paraphrase failures out of 27 on the first live run — the same constant-offset defect the v2 false-start change fixed, where noise that never varies hides real regressions. Verified the change is one-directional: genuine paraphrase, a dropped word, and a deleted 'not' are all still caught. v3 was never used for a reported monthly result, so no published figure is affected. No passage edited.
